thread:
maria_customer: Hey, we're seeing very high startup latency for model endpoints on our dedicated cluster starting ~2026-03-10. Several requests time out or take 8-12s to respond. sample request-id: req_20260310_9f2a3b. Can we get a repro collection?

emma_support: Sorry about that — we'll help. Can you share a minimal curl repro and one or two failing request IDs? Also which cluster/namespace?

maria_customer: Cluster: dedicated-us-west-2, namespace: tenant-phi. Minimal curl I used: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"X-Request-ID: req_20260310_9f2a3b\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` Response sometimes 200 after 10s, sometimes 504.

emma_support: Thanks. Raj / infra — can you collect pod logs + node GPU metrics for tenant-phi around 2026-03-10T14:20-14:40Z? We'll need `kubectl logs` for the model pods and `dmesg` and `journalctl` on the nodes.

raj_oncall: On it. Can the customer run a quick `kubectl get pods -n tenant-phi -o wide` so we can see which nodes the pods landed on?

maria_customer: Pasting output:
```
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP           NODE
model-server-phi-5d8f9db6b4-2qv9k       1/1     Running   0          12d   10.2.4.12    g4dn-12xlarge-03
model-server-phi-5d8f9db6b4-7mngp       0/1     Pending   0          5m    <none>       g4dn-12xlarge-07
router-phi-64f8c9d8b-pt2zj              1/1     Running   0          20d   10.2.4.10    g4dn-12xlarge-01
```

leo_infra: Looks like one pod stayed Pending. Could be GPU scheduling or device plugin issues. Raj, can you grab `kubectl describe pod model-server-phi-5d8f9db6b4-7mngp -n tenant-phi` and `kubectl describe node g4dn-12xlarge-07`? Also collect `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` from the node.

raj_oncall: Will run those now. Maria — if possible create a debug bundle with `redwoodctl debug bundle create --cluster dedicated-us-west-2 --namespace tenant-phi --since \"2026-03-10T14:10:00Z\" --until \"2026-03-10T14:50:00Z\" --include-nodes g4dn-12xlarge-07`. That gives us kube objects + node logs + GPU metrics. If you can't run that, let us know and we'll trigger server-side collection (may require SSH keys).

maria_customer: running it now, ETA ~2m

sre-bot: debug bundle job started (id: dbg-20260310-87a1). size estimate ~150MB.

hana_eng: If bundle comes back, pls include the model server logs around warmup: search for \"Warmup\" and \"KV cache\" and any `OOM` or `failed to allocate` lines. Also paste a snippet of `nvidia-smi` from the node showing processes. Example expected output:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.95.05    Driver Version: 525.95.05    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A10          On           | 00000000:AF:00.0     | N/A                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
| GPU   GI   CI        PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory     |
| 0      0    0      32145  C+G    model-server-phi               7128MiB        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

deploybot: debug bundle dbg-20260310-87a1 uploaded to s3://redwood-debug-bundles/dedicated-us-west-2/dbg-20260310-87a1.tar.gz :link:

emma_support: Got the bundle. Raj/leo/hana — I've shared temporary access. I pulled `model-server` logs: saw repeated lines: `Warmup completed in 9.6s; kv-cache miss ratio: 76%` and `failed to allocate tensor: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` ~14:22:10. Node logs show GPU driver reload around same time.

leo_infra: Node g4dn-12xlarge-07 shows device plugin crashloop at 14:21:45 -> kubelet restarted plugin, then pods rescheduled. That would explain Pending and cold start. Also GPU memory usage was high on other pods — possible noisy neighbor. We'll patch scheduling affinity to avoid noisy nodes for tenant-phi in short term.

maria_customer: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Any repro steps we should try locally?

emma_support: Repro steps for us were: (1) send 5 concurrent curl requests with same model and request header `X-Request-ID` spaced 100ms, (2) observe one pod hitting warmup + kv-cache fill causing 8-12s responses, (3) note node-level plugin restarts correlate with timeouts. Attached example curl loop:
```
for i in {1..5}; do \
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"X-Request-ID: repro_${i}\" -d '{\"input\":\"warmup test\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &\
done; wait
```

raj_oncall: For metrics we grabbed: GPU mem used spiked to 95% on g4dn-12xlarge-03 at 14:20:50 (other tenant pods), then device plugin process crashed on g4dn-12xlarge-07 due to transient driver fault. I've filed infra ticket INF-3487 to track driver update and eviction policy tweak.

hana_eng: We'll roll a hotfix to pre-warm KV cache during pod startup and reduce initial allocation to avoid full memory grab. We'll also add a Canary to avoid evicting tenant-phi onto nodes with high GPU pressure.

emma_support: Thanks all. Maria, we'll keep this thread updated as INF-3487 progresses. If you see regression after the infra patch, please re-run the curl loop and paste one request-id. :thumbsup:

maria_customer: Will do. Thanks everyone! :heart:
